labels.label: btzdef:btz_extension_btz_embedding
labels.notes: GX.IsBTZEmbedding = IsEmbedding ∧ IsE0Mor ι univ ∧ (range ι)ᶜ ⊆ S0 N carries the three printed conditions of l.325-327: embedding, a.e. morphism, complement of the image of type 𝔼₀. Nothing is silently dropped. The source M only needs ChartedSpace E0Y, which is more general than the paper. Two narrowings are disclosed and keep the row partial and unmarked: (a) 𝔼₀ instead of 𝔼_{≥0} (DEC-116 (b)/DEC-125), and (b) « a.e. 𝔼-morphism » read as IsE0Mor, a local structomorphism at every point, BTZ points included. That is stronger than l.359's definition (continuous, a (G,X)-morphism on dense locally connected opens of the regular parts), so IsBTZEmbedding is a narrower predicate than the printed one. The checklist marks it '⚠ read'. BTZExtension: N : E0Mfd (T2, second countable, E0Y-atlas in e0Groupoid; not connected, as at l.261). isBTZEmbedding_iff_injective is proved and true under the IsE0Mor reading. Module docstring: the six labels appear unmarked within the first 4000 characters (lines 10-19), and the module docstring carries no ``**`label`**``. Five declaration docstrings do use that form; see the findings.

labels.label: btzdef:common_sub_btz_extension
labels.notes: CommonSubBTZ i j has X : E0Mfd, a : M₀ → X, b : X → M₁, c : X → M₂, all three BTZ-embeddings, with b ∘ a = i and c ∘ a = j. That is the printed diagram (l.1305-1313). The paper's hypothesis that i and j are BTZ-extensions is dropped from the parameters. For a definition this is a disclosed generalisation (checklist '⚠ weakened'): when i and j are BTZ the structure is the paper's, and b ∘ a = i makes i BTZ anyway. CommonSubBTZ.base shows the type is inhabited.

labels.label: btzdef:morphism_common_sub_extension
labels.notes: IsMorphism = IsE0Mor φ univ ∧ Y.b ∘ φ = X.b ∧ Y.c ∘ φ = X.c, which is the printed diagram over M₁ and M₂ only. Equivalent = there is a bijective morphism (l.1330). The 𝔼≥0-morphism is read as IsE0Mor, the same reading as label 1, and is disclosed. The derived facts are all proved: injectivity, being a BTZ-embedding, commuting with a, uniqueness, and the inverse of a bijective morphism being a morphism, so Equivalent is an equivalence relation.

labels.label: btzdef:maximal_common_sub_btz_extension
labels.notes: IsMaximal X = ∀ Y, ∃ φ, Y.IsMorphism X φ ∧ Injective φ, which is l.1336 literally, injectivity included. The redundancy claim holds and is proved by isMaximal_iff through IsMorphism.injective (X.b ∘ φ = Y.b with Y.b injective). It needs nothing beyond the definition, so it also holds for the printed paper notion. IsMaximal.equivalent (two maximal ones are equivalent) is correct. The quantification is over carriers in Type: disclosed in the REPORT and harmless.

labels.label: btzdef:common_over_btz_extension
labels.notes: CommonOverBTZ i j has X : E0Mfd and BTZ-embeddings a : M₁ → X, b : M₂ → X with a ∘ i = b ∘ j, which is the printed diagram (l.1383-1393). i and j are generalised to arbitrary maps, as in label 2.

labels.label: btzdef:morphism_common_over_btz_extension
labels.notes: IsMorphism = IsE0Mor φ univ ∧ φ ∘ X.a = Y.a ∧ φ ∘ X.b = Y.b, and Equivalent = bijective morphism, as at l.1401 and l.1411. Injectivity is not required, as printed; the REPORT raises this as an open question, not as a defect. IsMorphism.unique (via density of range a) and the equivalence-relation facts are proved.

findings.what: GX.continuous_of_isE0Mor' duplicates GX.E0AbsMax.continuous_of_isE0Mor. The primed version is strictly more general: it needs no HasGroupoid N, and M is free of the section's T2/Connected/SecondCountable variables. There is no clash today, because the names (prime) and namespaces (GX vs GX.E0AbsMax) differ. At graduation into GX/BTZ/ it is a redundancy, not a collision. It would become ambiguous only if a later file opened E0AbsMax and someone dropped the prime.
findings.fix: At graduation, keep one lemma under a non-primed name, e.g. GX.IsE0Mor.continuous or the primed lemma renamed into GX.E0Spear, and make AbsMax's version an alias of it or delete it.
